records.summary: Murkwood is the Hist forest at the heart of Black Marsh, the legendary dark wood that ever moves, around Helstrom. Its people are the Root-Folk, its beasts are medusas and Naga, and outsiders who enter without leave do not come out.
records.landform: Low swamp forest of root-hummocks, braided river arms and black Heart-Mud flats, with a few dry rises.
records.biome: Dense Hist swamp forest of great roots and hanging moss, black Heart-Mud flats and slow rivers
records.climate: Hot, humid and overcast, with flesh-fly clouds in the warm months and heavy monsoon rain from late spring.

notes.text: Murkwood is the legendary dark forest that ever moves, on a river deep in the swamps of Black Marsh and home to many medusas. Canon has the Conclave of Baal at Stormhold find where it stands by reading the Elder Scrolls with an ancient tablet; our map shows where it stands in 4E 201, around Helstrom.

In the Imperial Simulacrum of 3E 399 Jagar Tharn hid a piece of the Staff of Chaos in Murkwood, and the Eternal Champion fetched it. The forest has moved many times since; Helstrom and the Root-Folk have stood beside it through all of them.
In 4E 201 the forest crowds the river arms around Helstrom, held by the Root-Folk, the Hutan-Tzel at its west edge, and several camps of Naga and Paatru. Few outsiders come, and fewer come back.
The Root-Folk of Helstrom (Saxhleel) hold the heart; the Hutan-Tzel hold the west; tribeless Naga and the toad-like Paatru hold the camps at the margin.
Fellrunner feathers, sap, eggs, hides and river fish; farmers trade sacks of feathers to hunters, and a single armband of the pale down lets a hunter move through Murkwood undetected.
The Hist: every settlement sends its people to a village tree to hatch and bury. The Root Talk at Helstrom is the occasion on which the tribes hear the trees speak.
A dark wood of huge roots, hanging moss and black water; light comes green and dim, the air is thick and loud with insects, and the forest never looks the same twice.
Medusas in the deep wood, Naga ambushes on the river arms, Paatru who kill on sight, and the moving wood itself, which can swallow a path overnight.
Low, wet ground cut by braided river arms flowing toward the lake, with dry rises where the roots hold the soil. Heart-Mud flats lie on the south.
Great Hist trees, mosses and ferns; fellrunners, medusas, rootworms, crocodiles, flesh-flies and torchbugs. Fellrunner pale down is the region's famous good.
Hot, wet and still; monsoon in late spring and early summer; fog in the early mornings and a perpetual warmth.

records.summary: Lake Ulaish is the great lake south-east of Helstrom where the interior waters pool before running to Lilmoth and Blackrose. Fishing hamlets, a toll fort and a trading city share its shores, and boats are its roads.
records.landform: A broad shallow lake with silt islets, reed shores and river deltas at its north-west corner.
records.biome: Shallow freshwater lake, reed beds, silt islets and delta marsh
records.climate: Humid and warm, with squalls across open water and monsoon flooding of the shores.

notes.text: Lake Ulaish is the large lake south-east of Helstrom where the river arms of the interior spread out and slow before moving on. UESP has no page for it; the name is Project Tamriel's.

records.summary: Aunike Ridge is the long rise of drier ground west and south-west of Helstrom, with two peaks and a few Chime-Keeper hamlets. It is the interior's rare high ground and the line between the Hist forest and the Paatru country.
records.landform: A long low ridge of firm ground, rock outcrops and two summits, among reed marsh.
records.biome: Upland marsh ridge of rock outcrop, scrub, reed and a few stunted trees
records.climate: Warmer and drier than the forest, with steady breeze on the summits and monsoon rain from the north.

notes.text: Aunike Ridge is a ridge of firm ground west and south-west of Helstrom, with two marked peaks and two Chime-Keeper hamlets. UESP has no page for it; the name is Project Tamriel's.

sources.title: Lore:Aunike Ridge (no page)
sources.locator: UESP search and page lookup, 2026-11-08: no Lore page for Aunike Ridge

notes.text: Nothing is recorded. The Kothringi-named hamlets on it, Nacydes and Tydeos, are read as Kothringi places resettled by Argonians after 2E 560 because the ridge is dry.
In 4E 201 its hamlets keep watch from the peaks and trade chimes for hides with the Paatru camp to the west; Naga bands of Salt-Tooth Camp range across it.
Chime-Keepers at Nacydes and Tydeos; Paatru and Naga hold the camps at its margin.
Lizard-herding, hides, hunting and tin chimes traded with the Paatru, with Helstrom's levy and with Korydon.
Sithis and a quiet Dibella among the Chime-Keepers; watchfires on the peaks are a small offering to the Hist.
Rock outcrops and grass-scrub above the reeds, stone-footed huts, windchimes, watchfires at night and wide views over the marsh.
Naga and Paatru raiders, ridge cats, falls on the summit paths, and cold wind at night on the open top.
A long spine of firm ground rising from marsh, with rock outcrops, two summits, steep faces on the north and shelving slopes on the south.
Grass, scrub, stunted trees and lizards; ridge cats and marsh-lizard herds; fewer insects than the forest.
Breezy and a little drier than the forest, with morning mist and monsoon rain from the north.

records.summary: The Ultherus Swamp is the great wetland south of Helstrom, in which the Kothringi-named town of Korydon lies. Canon says little of it except that the lovely and deadly dragon's-tongue is especially common there.
records.landform: A low wet maze of channels, hummocks and cattail beds, with rings of firmer ground.
records.biome: Cattail and reed swamp with dragon's-tongue beds, hummocks and braided channels
records.climate: Hot, humid and heavy, with monsoon rain and constant insects.

notes.text: The Ultherus Swamp, also written Utherus, is a region of Black Marsh of which little is known; the beautiful but deadly dragon's-tongue plant is especially common there. In our map it lies south of Helstrom around Korydon.
Canon records nothing. The Kothringi-named towns here, Korydon, Myroleon, Nemeon, are read as old Kothringi places that Argonians resettled after the Knahaten Flu of 2E 560.
In 4E 201 the swamp is crossed by boat; Korydon's Chime-Keepers harvest the dragon's-tongue, Tumnatu hunters keep to the reeds, and a Root-Folk waystation sits at its south.
The Chime-Keepers of Korydon, Nemeon and Myroleon, Tumnatu hunters, and a few Root-Folk boatmen.
Dragon's-tongue and other swamp herbs, chimes, rope and boats from Korydon, fish, and pelts traded north to Helstrom and south to Blackrose.
Sithis and the Hist; Korydon adds Z'en and Dibella, kept at a chime-hung shrine.
A grey-green maze of cattails, reed and black water, with rings of dry ground and stilt towns hung with metal chimes.
Dragon's-tongue patches that kill the careless, deep-water predators, Tumnatu parties and fog-bound channels that lose boats.
Flat and low, cut by many channels, with ring-like firm ground such as the one under Korydon; the south opens into the larger waters toward Blackrose.
Dragon's-tongue, cattails, reed, water-lilies; eels, crocodiles, marsh-lizards and swarms of flesh-flies.
Hot and heavy, with monsoon from late spring to summer and a persistent warm fog on the channels.
